title: OpenClaw
summary: The operating layer for agents, memory, tools, messaging, and human-in-the-loop work.
problem: Delegated agent work needs continuity, tools, memory, and human review boundaries to become operationally useful.
howItWorks: OpenClaw connects agents to workspace files, skills, messaging, tasks, and runtime context so work can move through explicit handoffs.
proof: Active operating layer for SIndustries agents, task execution, daily ops note capture, weekly content review workflows, and multi-agent content operations — Quinn orchestrates, Ivy authors, Tom approves, Lobster merges. The SIndustries skill library has grown with spec-author, website-content, and operating-notes skills, and spec authoring for the bookmark pipeline is now heartbeat-queued through OpenClaw for auditable, rate-controlled LLM work.

title: X bookmark reviews
summary: A pipeline for turning saved signals into reviews, specs, tasks, and decisions.
problem: Useful external signals are easy to save and hard to convert into action.
howItWorks: Bookmarks are reviewed, grouped, evaluated for usefulness, and promoted into specs or tasks when they warrant action. Ingestion now routes through the OpenClaw gateway for telemetry and cost visibility, scripts have been consolidated into the agents/workflows/bookmark/ skill pattern, spec generation is heartbeat-queued so LLM work is auditable and rate-controlled, and a review-state dashboard tracks review state, spec generation, and approvals in one view.
proof: Pipeline now produces review state, implementation specs, task proposals, and a review-state dashboard. Spec generation is heartbeat-queued and gateway-routed ingestion is in place.

title: Tasks API
summary: Task state, ownership, comments, reviews, and heartbeat-driven operating discipline.
problem: Agent work needs a shared source of truth for ownership, status, review, and handoff.
howItWorks: The Tasks API tracks tasks, comments, tags, readiness, and status transitions for SIndustries work.
proof: SIndustries tasks are tracked through the API and driven by agent heartbeat and cron workflows. Task history shipped across the API, schema, and UI tab. Task automation tooling is now maintained in the SIndustries repo as the canonical location.

title: Design System
summary: Reusable visual language, components, and constraints for SIndustries products.
problem: A product studio needs visual consistency without slowing down small experiments.
howItWorks: Shared tokens, components, and design constraints keep new surfaces coherent while remaining easy to ship.
proof: The Pencil design token package, sync checks, and @sindustries/ui integration are shipped, with a dark theme enabled. The website uses shared design tokens and reusable card-stack components.

title: Content Factory
summary: A system that turns daily operational signals into published website content — without manual coordination.
problem: Building a product studio generates constant signal: shipped work, decisions, experiments, lessons. None of it reaches a public audience unless someone manually converts notes into content. That conversion was the bottleneck.
howItWorks: Daily signals are captured automatically as work happens. Each week, those notes are distilled into a structured review that identifies what's worth publishing and who needs to approve it. Content tasks are created automatically, assigned for authoring, and tracked through a review-and-merge workflow. Ops activity becomes public signal on a weekly cadence, with a single human approval step.
proof: Pipeline shipped 2026-06-01. First full content cycle completed end-to-end on 2026-06-04: Quinn orchestration, Ivy authoring, Tom approval, and Lobster auto-merge.
